title: How to Make a TikTok Ad for Your Store | AIVideosUGC
description: How to make a TikTok ad from a product link or one photo. You get a script, a spoken voice, words on screen, and a file you can post on TikTok.
h1: How to Make a TikTok Ad When You've Never Made One
lead: You get a tall TikTok ad that opens on your product and gives one reason to buy. Paste the product page or start from a photo. The script, a voiceover, captions, and a track you can post come back with the file.
summary: You leave with one reason to buy, a vertical clip that opens on the product, a voice, captions, and a small first campaign you control.

sections.h2: What a First TikTok Ad Includes
paras: You need one product and one reason someone would buy it, and the first file is ready without a filming appointment.
A key finder that clips onto a bag is a real shot. Pair it with a track buyers still hear this week, and say how it clips on.
Record a short clip of your own voice if you want the shop to sound like you. Otherwise pick a generated voice and rewrite the line until it sounds like something you would say at the counter.
A file you can publish. Captions, the tall shape, and a track from the ad music library come with the video. Send it to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram, or download it and post it yourself.
sections.alt: Adult woman applies cream from a plain light-peach tube to her cheek at the seaside.

paras: Three moves, and you have a file without a studio day or an empty editing screen.
Paste the page when it shows the item you ship. A phone-stand page that leads with the folded thickness is enough. You can fix a wrong title before the job starts.
Or upload one photo and one sentence about the action. Save the price for the editor, where you add it later.
A sample you can echo: a hand unfolds a slim phone stand on a cafe table in soft daylight. Write the same kind of sentence for your item.
A product link and a photo each have a door. Use [URL to video](page:url-to-video) when you start from a product link. Use [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) when you start from a photo.
You choose the person before you write the line, so the words fit that person. A product-only frame works too. See the [actor library](page:ai-actors).
The person on screen goes by a name you chose for the shop.
Play the tall file on your phone, then put the price in the editor. The price has to match what the shopper pays. After that, publish to TikTok or keep the download.
A shop system can start that same job through an API when a new listing goes up.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube over a blank notebook on a bright cafe table.

sections.h2: Why Skip the Film Crew for Version One
paras: The opening shows the product doing something a shopper can recognize.
A first version can be a hand zipping a pouch, a drink poured over ice, or a shoe turned to show the sole. Those scenes are ready without an influencer on the call sheet.
The second opening can be a different first line on the same cream photo. You get that line without booking another morning.
A shop that also sells in Mexico can keep the cream scene and replace the spoken line with Spanish. That is another file, and the scene stays the one you already have.
sections.alt: Two adult hands spread white cream from a plain peach tube across the back of a hand.

paras: The product is on screen in the opening, while the shopper is still watching.
Keep the mug photo. For the next file, change only who speaks. A new first line is a different test, and it belongs in its own file.

Match the length to the motion. Six seconds fits one motion. Ten fits a short demo. Fifteen fits a simple sequence. Thirty fits a longer one. A video is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30.
Captions and the song live in this editor. When the words sit clear of the mug, this pass is done. A new shape, such as a square for a feed, is a separate job.
sections.alt: Adult hands turn one plain peach sunscreen tube for a pre-launch check.

sections.h2: Where the First File Goes Next
paras: The tall file is ready for TikTok, and each other placement gets the shape it actually plays, as its own file.
TikTok gets the 9:16 file, with the product on screen in the opening moments. The [TikTok ads](page:plat-tiktok) page has the size detail.
Instagram Reels plays that same tall shape, full screen. [Instagram](page:plat-instagram) covers the feed next to Reels.
Facebook Reels stays tall, and the feed gets a square, 1:1. Keep every card in a swipeable row the same shape. See [Facebook](page:plat-facebook).
YouTube Shorts uses 9:16 again, with the words in the middle, clear of the bottom and the right edge. [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts) is where this shape is used.
A product page on your store can hold the video where shoppers land next.
A listing can show the same product facts in a video, beside the still. Those are two jobs. Sizes for every placement are in [ad sizes by platform](page:guide-ad-sizes-by-platform).
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube beside a notebook on a bright desk.

sections.h2: How a Shop Uses the First Ad
paras: A candle shop pastes the product link and gets a tall video of the lid coming off.
A plant shop opens on the leaves, with the pot large enough to see.
A drink shop writes the price and the line in the editor, and picks a song for the clip.
A pet shop posts the file from the listing photo it already has.
A fashion shop publishes the file to TikTok and downloads a copy for Facebook and Instagram.
A supplement shop shows the same offer to the same people on the same ad budget, and waits a few days before deciding.
A home shop keeps the words in the middle, clear of the buttons on the right.
A beauty shop starts from a still photo and one sentence, then checks the shade against the real bottle.
A jewelry shop adds a voiceover and reads every word before it launches.
A gadget shop lets its listing system start the video through an API when a new product goes up.
You post one product and one reason to buy, in a 9:16 video that starts with the action. Add a script, a voiceover, captions, and a song.
The cost shows before the job starts. If a job fails, the credits come back. The download has no watermark.
sections.alt: One adult hand smooths white cream along a forearm beside a plain peach tube.

faq.q: How do I make a TikTok video ad?
faq.a: A tool that starts from your product and returns a tall, captioned clip with a voice. The guide covers each step, from the link to the file you post.

faq.q: How do I make the TikTok ad look like my shop?
faq.a: Start from your product photo or page, pick an AI actor or none, and set the line, the colors, and the captions so the ad looks like your shop.

faq.q: How long does a first TikTok ad take to make?
faq.a: You stay at the keyboard for one pass. Paste the page for the wool scarf, or upload the photo, and type the weave in one sentence. The tall file comes back with the spoken line.

faq.q: How does a product page become a TikTok video?
faq.a: A page that shows the kettle can be the start. You write one sentence about the pour, and you decide whether a person is in the frame. The file is tall.

faq.q: What does a TikTok ad generator create?
faq.a: A tall file built from the product you already sell. For a leather belt, the buckle is on screen and a voice says what it does. The studio day can wait until you know which opening people watch.

faq.q: Can these ads stand in for a traditional shoot?
faq.a: Use them when you are still choosing the opening. A filmed spot with someone you hired can stay the main film. The generated file is there so you can learn which first line people watch, before you book that day.

faq.q: What do I gain by making the TikTok ad this way?
faq.a: You find out whether the buckle is a clear opening before you book anyone. The belt photo you already have is the raw material. A weak opening shows up in the file, while the crew day is still unbooked.

faq.q: Can I aim different versions at different audiences?
faq.a: Yes. One file can speak to people who commute, and another can speak to people who work at a desk. Keep the candle the same, and change who the line is for. Your ad account tells you which file they watched.

faq.q: Can I match my brand's look?
faq.a: Yes. A navy caption and your own spoken line are enough for a honey shop to look like itself. The file should still look like it belongs on a phone, with the jar large enough to see.
